question: Pipe A alone can fill a tank in 8 hours. Pipe B alone can fill it in 6 hours. If both the pipes are opened and after 2 hours pipe A is closed, then pipe B will fill the remaining tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Capacity** of the tank (LCM of 8 and 6) = **24 units**.

**Efficiency** of Pipe A = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units/hr and Pipe B = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 units/hr.

**Work done** in 2 hours by (A + B) = (3 + 4) × 2 = **14 units**.

**Remaining Work** = 24 − 14 = 10 units.

Time taken by **Pipe B** for remaining part = 10 ÷ 4 = **2 (1/2) hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 (1)/(2) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Pipe A** = 8 hr

Time taken by **Pipe B** = 6 hr

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

⇒ **Combined efficiency** of Pipe A and Pipe B = 3 + 4 = **7 units/hr**.

⇒ **Work done** in 2 hours = 7 units/hr × 2 hr = **14 units**.

⇒ **Remaining tank** to be filled = 24 − 14 = **10 units**.

⇒ Since **Pipe A** is closed, **Pipe B** fills the rest.

⇒ Time taken by **Pipe B** = 10 units ÷ 4 units/hr = 2.5 hr.

⇒ 2.5 hr = **2 (1/2) hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 (1)/(2) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a pipe takes 'x' hours to fill a tank, its 1-hour work is 1/x of the tank.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes (filling) have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (emptying) have negative efficiency in the total work calculation.

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

Total capacity is usually taken as the LCM of the individual times to simplify calculations into integer efficiency values.</p
